subject: Private deployment evidence & license-scope checklist for MedTech (MSA + OF)
messages:
From: Caleb Murphy <caleb.murphy@medtech.co>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medtech.co; security@medtech.co
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment evidence & license-scope questions (MedTech)

Hi Markus / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and security at MedTech are starting the legal/evidence intake for an on-prem deployment. A few asks up front so we can scope our SOW/order form and legal review: 

1) License scope: we need explicit language that allows us to run a pinned model version on-prem (single-customer instance) with local KV cache retention disabled by default. Can you confirm the license granularity (per-seat / per-instance / per-core)?

2) Audit / evidence: our security team expects a mechanism similar to an escrow or source-deposit to validate continuity of service in the event Redwood becomes unavailable. They are open to a staged approach (metadata + signed binary + controlled source deposit). Please indicate what you can provide and timelines.

3) Onsite / remote audit windows: we typically request a once-per-year technical review plus a one-time onboarding evidence package (SOC/Sec artifacts, attestation). What notice and lead time do you need?

4) Order form: can you share the private deployment excerpt (how addendum references MSA, support SLAs, and indemnity points)?

I've attached our high-level security questionnaire to help guide responses. Would prefer a short phone call next week to line up owners and a target delivery date for the evidence pack.

Thanks,
Caleb
Head of Procurement — MedTech Inc.
Attachment: MedTech_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Caleb Murphy <caleb.murphy@medtech.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & license-scope questions (MedTech)

Hi Caleb — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (sales lead), Aditya (legal), and Neha (deploy eng) so we can coordinate. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Quick answers
- License granularity: Redwood prefers a per-instance + capacity metric (reserved GPUs / vCPU equivalent). We can map to a per-instance fee in the OF and include a short definition in the private deployment addendum.
- Escrow-like option: we can offer a staged evidence deposit (attestation + signed runtime binaries + controlled-source escrow on a 3rd-party hold). Need legal to confirm exact wording.
- Audit windows: standard is annual remote review + one-time onboarding evidence package. Typical notice for remote reviews: 30–45 days. Onsite audits require SLA exceptions and may be limited to redacted logs.

Requested items from your side to scope deliverables
- Prioritized checklist from security (we saw the questionnaire; if you can highlight top 7 must-haves, that accelerates delivery).
- Target handover date for onboarding package.

Action items / timeline (proposed)
1) Legal redline exchange (we can share our suggested addendum language by EOD Wednesday) — Aditya
2) Technical evidence mapping & sample files — Neha (ready in 7 business days once we have the checklist)
3) Sync call to align on audit scope & order form — propose Tue 9/1 or Wed 9/2 (30 min)

If that works I will send a calendar invite.

— Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>; Caleb Murphy <caleb.murphy@medtech.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & license-scope questions (MedTech)

Markus / Caleb —

High-level legal positions we intend to propose in the MSA addendum / order form: 

1) License scope: define "Instance" and map to reserved-capacity unit. Include permitted-use clause for customer production workloads and an explicit prohibition on multi-tenant resale.
2) Escrow / source-deposit: we prefer a staged escrow approach — (a) signed runtime artifacts + attestations delivered to an agreed custodian; (b) critical build scripts and limited source under mutual NDA and post-termination release conditions. Avoid open-source-style public source escrow.
3) Audit access: remote technical evidence deliverable + on-prem inspection subject to redacted logs and non-disruptive constraints. Any onsite audit requires 30 days' notice and an agreed scope of systems (no source code server access without a court/contractual trigger).
4) SLA & remedy: propose credits for SLA failures; exclude long-tail liability for third-party infra.

I'll prepare a tracked redline and an excerpt of suggested OF language and drop it in the drive link below by EOD Monday. If you anticipate MedTech pushing for broader source escrow (full source release), let me know — we'll need a commercial concession or escrow escrow-agent language.

Attachment: RF_license_redline.docx
Drive: https://drive.redwoodinc/review/privdeploy-redline-2026

-Aditya
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Caleb Murphy <caleb.murphy@medtech.co>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>; Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, security@medtech.co; procurement@medtech.co
Date: 2026-09-01T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & license-scope questions (MedTech)

Thanks Aditya — that helps. A couple clarifications from our end after an internal sync: 

- MedTech position on deposit: we are likely to accept staged escrow but will insist on a mechanism that guarantees recovery of a runnable artifact (not just metadata). We are open to a process where Redwood provides: (i) signed runtime binaries and checksums, (ii) a limited set of build scripts under escrow, and (iii) an attestation of the build process.
- Audit frequency: annual remote review is fine; we also expect a one-time onboarding window with evidence delivered before go-live.
- Notice: 30–60 days is acceptable; we prefer 45 days for remote reviews.

Open asks: 
- Can Redwood include a clause that permits a mutually-agreed third-party custodian for the staged deposit?
- What is Redwood's standard turnaround for producing the onboarding evidence pack (once we provide the prioritized questionnaire items)?

I've attached a short draft (audit scope + expectations) to highlight what our security team will expect. Happy to walk through on the call — Tue 9/1 at 9:00 PT works for us.

-Caleb
Attachment: MedTech_Audit_Scope.docx
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Caleb Murphy <caleb.murphy@medtech.co>

Date: 2026-09-02T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & license-scope questions (MedTech)

Caleb — appreciate the clarifications. Quick confirmation of next steps from Redwood side before the call tomorrow: 

1) Legal redline (Aditya) — we will upload the proposed MSA addendum + OF excerpt to the drive and share via DocuSign preview by EOD today. Expect language for: instance definition, permitted use, staged escrow via mutually-agreed custodian, and audit limitations.
2) Technical evidence (Neha) — once MedTech flags the top 7 items in the questionnaire, we will assemble the onboarding pack within 7 business days (attestations + signed artifacts + sample config files). Onsite/inspection requests will be treated case-by-case.
3) Commercial mapping (Laura / Markus) — we will include a private-deploy order form excerpt showing reserved capacity bands and predictable support SLAs (SLA credit language to be included).

I'll send the calendar invite for Tue 9/1 09:00 PT and attach a short excerpt of the order form we typically use for private deployments so you can preview the OF scoping language.

Regards,
— Markus
